title: Optics Still Driving Marvell’s AI Business More Than Custom Chips
gist: Marvell's datacenter/AI business now drives ~79-89% of total revenue, but within that AI mix electro-optical components (~$1.4B/quarter, +97.2% YoY) still dwarf custom XPU/CPU silicon (~$425M/quarter, +43.1% YoY) despite market hype around AWS/Google custom-chip deals, and management keeps raising FY2027-FY2028 guidance sharply.

themes.theme: Optics, not custom silicon, still leads Marvell's AI story

insights.claim: At Marvell, optical components for AI networks and switching are generating more revenue than the custom AI chip (XPU/CPU) business that draws most investor and press attention.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: Investors overweighting the custom-silicon narrative (AWS/Google deals) may be mispricing where Marvell's actual current revenue and growth are concentrated.
insights.quote: Optical components for networks as well as switching are still driving the bulk of the sales.
insights.locator: opening paragraph

insights.claim: Marvell's AI business began in early 2023 (Q1 FY2024) at roughly $77 million, split between about $12 million in early custom ASIC sales (via the AWS Graviton deal) and about $66 million in electro-optics, showing optics led the AI ramp from the start.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: Establishes the historical baseline showing optics-led growth is not a recent shift but the pattern since Marvell's AI business began.
insights.locator: AI business as GenAI boom began

insights.claim: In Marvell's Q2 FY2027 (ended August 1, 2026), electro-optical component revenue was an estimated $1.4 billion, up 97.2% year on year, remaining the dominant piece of the AI revenue story.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: Optics revenue growth (97.2% YoY) is outpacing custom XPU growth (43.1% YoY), making optics the higher-growth, larger-dollar AI segment right now.
insights.locator: electro-optical components continue to dominate

insights.claim: Custom AI XPU sales at Marvell were an estimated $425 million in Q2 FY2027, down slightly sequentially but up 43.1% year on year, beating the roughly 20% growth rate Marvell had previously guided Wall Street to expect.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: Custom silicon growth is accelerating faster than prior guidance, a positive read-through for the AWS/Google custom chip pipeline even though it remains smaller than optics.
insights.locator: AI XPU sales slumped a little sequentially

insights.claim: Non-AI datacenter product revenue at Marvell fell an estimated 28.4% to about $347 million in Q2 FY2027, indicating legacy datacenter demand is shrinking as AI-related products dominate the segment.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: Signals that within "datacenter," non-AI product lines are actively declining, reinforcing that Marvell's growth story is now almost entirely AI-dependent.
insights.locator: other datacenter products sold outside of the AI customer set

insights.claim: By Q2 FY2027, Marvell's total estimated AI revenue reached $1.82 billion, up 90.9% year on year and 23.6 times higher than roughly three years earlier.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: Quantifies the scale of Marvell's AI ramp (23.6x in three years) as a reference point for modeling forward growth durability.
insights.locator: Fast forward to Q2 F2027

themes.theme: Datacenter now dominates, legacy chip business fading

insights.claim: Marvell's datacenter product sales in Q2 FY2027 were $2.17 billion, up 45.7% year on year and up 18.5% sequentially.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: Core headline growth metric confirming datacenter is Marvell's primary growth engine.
insights.locator: second quarter of fiscal 2027

insights.claim: The datacenter segment now accounts for 79.3% of Marvell's total sales; including legacy enterprise networking (which the author argues should arguably be grouped with datacenter), it rises to 89% of total revenue.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: Marvell has effectively become an AI/datacenter pure-play; legacy diversification (telco, consumer, industrial) is now immaterial to the investment thesis.
insights.locator: datacenter part of the Marvell business is now 79.3 percent

insights.claim: Marvell's datacenter business has grown 8.1x since Q2 FY2021, while its legacy chip businesses (telco, enterprise networking, consumer/industrial) have grown only 1.3x over the same period.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: Illustrates the structural bifurcation of Marvell's business: legacy segments are essentially flat/low-growth while AI/datacenter compounds rapidly, justifying a re-rating toward an AI-infrastructure multiple.
insights.locator: datacenter business has grown a factor of 8.1X

insights.claim: Combined legacy chip businesses (telco/carrier, enterprise networking, consumer/industrial) rose 10.1% in the quarter to $567.8 million, a much slower growth rate than the AI-driven datacenter business.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: Confirms legacy segments are still growing modestly but are increasingly irrelevant to the overall growth trajectory.
insights.locator: legacy businesses up, and they rose by 10.1 percent

insights.claim: Marvell is behaving like Nvidia, lumping all non-datacenter business into a single vague category (Marvell's legacy grouping mirrors Nvidia's "Edge Computing" grouping), and the resulting revenue chart shape resembles Nvidia's own divisional split before and after the GenAI boom.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: Suggests Marvell may be early in a similar re-rating trajectory to Nvidia's post-GenAI divisional transformation, worth tracking for multiple expansion.
insights.locator: this chart looks very much like Nvidia’s chart

insights.claim: Marvell is positioning itself as a counterbalance to Nvidia's dominance in GenAI infrastructure, in the same competitive role as Broadcom, as AI networking and custom XPUs/CPUs grow among hyperscalers, cloud builders, and AI model builders.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: Frames Marvell alongside Broadcom as the key custom-silicon/networking beneficiaries of hyperscalers diversifying away from pure Nvidia GPU dependence.
insights.quote: Marvell is becoming every bit as much of a counter balance to Nvidia’s largesse in GenAI as is Broadcom.
insights.locator: Nvidia, for what it is worth, has done the same thing

insights.claim: Marvell has not disclosed explicit segment/division revenue breakdowns since Q3 FY2026, forcing the author to build an estimated model of the divisions; the author flags these estimates as increasingly uncertain ("guesswork") absent clearer company disclosure.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: All specific dollar figures attributed to Marvell's internal segments in this piece are analyst estimates, not company-reported numbers, and carry real estimation risk for investors relying on them.
insights.quote: the error bars on these estimated division sales are getting fuzzier and fuzzier
insights.locator: Unless Marvell talks about these explicitly

insights.claim: The author argues the SEC should require companies to report financial segments matching how they are actually run and discussed internally, implicitly criticizing Marvell (and by extension other AI infrastructure suppliers) for reduced external segment disclosure as their AI businesses scale.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: Flags a governance/disclosure risk theme relevant across AI infrastructure suppliers: reduced segment reporting increases the modeling uncertainty investors face when valuing AI-exposed revenue streams.
insights.quote: The US Securities and Exchange Commission should have rules about when a business that is clearly comprised of divisions needs to be financially reported as such.
insights.locator: SEC should have rules

insights.claim: Marvell's acquisitions of IBM's custom chip business (via GlobalFoundries), Inphi, and Celestica AI, combined with its sale of the automotive chip business to Infineon, were strategic moves that positioned the company to concentrate on the AI/GenAI opportunity.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: Marvell's current AI leverage is the direct result of a multi-year M&A strategy (buying custom-silicon/optics capability, shedding automotive) rather than organic pivoting alone.
insights.locator: Imagine if Marvell had not bought IBM’s custom chip business

insights.claim: The author predicts Marvell will likely continue divesting non-AI divisions to raise cash and sharpen its focus on the GenAI opportunity.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: Investors should watch for further Marvell divestitures of legacy units as a signal of continued AI-focused capital reallocation.
insights.quote: It will not be surprising if Marvell sells off other divisions to get cash for maneuvering room and to have better focus.
insights.locator: It's all hands on the GenAI deck

themes.theme: Q2 FY2027 profitability and balance sheet

insights.claim: Marvell's total Q2 FY2027 revenue was $2.74 billion (up 36.5%), with operating income of $460 million (up 58.5%) and net income of $308 million (up 58.1%) — profitability grew faster than revenue, indicating operating leverage as the AI mix rises.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: Margin expansion alongside strong revenue growth suggests Marvell's AI-heavy mix is structurally more profitable, supporting further multiple re-rating if the trend holds.
insights.locator: Add it all up, and Marvell had $2.74 billion in revenues

insights.claim: Marvell holds $3.93 billion in cash, which the company says it needs to fulfill its obligations to the customers whose custom chips it is shepherding through design and production.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: Marvell's cash position is explicitly tied to funding customer chip programs (e.g., AWS, Google), a working-capital dynamic investors should factor into balance-sheet analysis of custom-silicon suppliers.
insights.locator: company has $3.93 billion in the bank

themes.theme: Forward guidance: accelerating growth through FY2029

insights.claim: Marvell guided Q3 FY2027 revenue to about $3.15 billion (up 51.8% year on year, up 15% sequentially); CEO Matt Murphy said growth will accelerate further in Q4 FY2027, and the first revenues from Google's recently expanded partnership with Marvell begin in Q3 FY2027.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: The Google partnership ramp is an imminent, identifiable revenue catalyst starting Q3 FY2027 — a concrete event to watch for confirmation of the custom-silicon growth thesis.
insights.locator: Notably, the first revenues from Google’s recently announced expanded partnership

insights.claim: Marvell's datacenter segment is expected to grow around 20% sequentially and about 75% year on year in Q3 FY2027.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: Confirms near-term datacenter growth is expected to further accelerate beyond the already-strong Q2 pace.
insights.locator: datacenter business is expected to grow by around 20 percent sequentially

insights.claim: Marvell raised its fiscal 2027 total revenue guidance to $12 billion, up from $11.5 billion a quarter prior, implying Q4 FY2027 revenue of roughly $3.7 billion, up 66.4% year on year.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: Sequential guidance raises across consecutive quarters indicate management confidence and momentum that is being repeatedly under-forecast by prior guidance.
insights.locator: Murphy sweetened the fiscal 2027 year’s revenues to $12 billion

insights.claim: For fiscal 2027, custom CPU/XPU sales are expected to total about $2 billion, growing around 33% — well ahead of the roughly 20% growth Marvell had previously guided — while the legacy comms/other chip business is expected to grow only about 10%.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: Custom silicon growth guidance is being raised faster than legacy segments, reinforcing the bifurcated growth thesis and giving investors a specific FY2027 custom-chip revenue target ($2B) to track.
insights.locator: custom CPUs and XPUs will represent about $2 billion in sales

insights.claim: Marvell raised its fiscal 2028 revenue guidance by $1.5 billion to $18 billion (a 50% growth rate), with the datacenter business projected to grow more than 60% and the custom CPU/XPU business expected to more than double in FY2028, growing even faster in FY2029, driven partly by the Google deal and by chip programs Marvell is shepherding for AWS and others.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: A $18 billion FY2028 revenue target with custom silicon more than doubling gives investors a concrete multi-year benchmark to hold management accountable to as the Google and AWS custom-chip programs scale.
insights.locator: Murphy upped the guidance by $1.5 billion

insights.claim: Scale-up network components for UALink, ESUN, and NVSwitch fabrics, plus the Celestial AI optical interposer, are expected to generate on the order of $300 million, with Celestial AI's hardware alone representing about $150 million of that figure.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: Identifies Celestial AI's optical interposer partnership as a specific, quantifiable emerging revenue line within Marvell's broader networking/scale-up business to track going forward.
insights.locator: Scale up network components for UALink, ESUN, and NVSwitch
